subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 9
summary: Axis Bank's fee hike wave continues across fourteen more cards, two Pine Labs and Retailio co-branded HDFC cards are discontinued, and Amex reveals a ₹66,000 annual fee on its flagship Platinum Card alongside a ₹60,000 welcome gift.
body_html:
Yesterday's Axis Bank fee wave continues today across fourteen more cards, same pattern: late fee tiers restructured and the DCC markup more than doubling. Two co-branded HDFC cards were also marked discontinued, and Amex made two premium-card moves worth knowing about even if you'll never hold either one. Axis first, since it's most of today's list, then HDFC, then Amex.

Axis Bank Vistara Infinite Credit Card

The ₹1,200 late fee, which used to apply to any total payment due above ₹10,000, now applies only to the ₹10,001-₹50,000 band, with a new ₹1,300 tier above that.

The catch: if your dues regularly cross ₹50,000, you're now paying more than before. Under ₹50,000, the fee is unchanged.

Kwik Axis Bank Credit Card

Same tier restructuring: a new ₹1,300 fee applies above ₹50,000 in dues, alongside the existing bands below it.

The catch: this only costs you extra if your outstanding due is regularly above ₹50,000.

AXIS BANK VISTARA SIGNATURE Credit Card

Same change as the Vistara Infinite card above: the ₹1,200 fee now applies specifically to the ₹10,001-₹50,000 band, with ₹1,300 kicking in above that.

The catch: identical, this bites only above ₹50,000 in dues.

Axis Bank Freecharge Credit Card

Full standard pattern: ₹1,200 for ₹10,001-₹50,000, ₹1,300 above ₹50,000, and the DCC markup up from 1.5% to 3.5% plus taxes.

The catch: the usual condition, this only matters if you carry a balance or spend through DCC-billed transactions.

LIC Axis Bank Signature Credit Card

Only the DCC markup changed here, 1.5% to 3.5% on international transactions billed in Indian currency. Late fee tiers untouched.

The catch: matters only if you spend abroad or through DCC-billed merchants.

Fibe Axis Bank Credit Card

Standard pattern applied: overdue penalty tiers restructured with the new ₹1,300 band above ₹50,000, and DCC markup raised to 3.5%.

The catch: as with the rest of today's Axis cards, a cost only for balance-carriers and DCC spenders.

Axis Bank Shoppers Stop Credit Card

Standard pattern: ₹1,200 for ₹10,001-₹50,000, ₹1,300 above ₹50,000, DCC markup to 3.5%.

The catch: the usual, this costs you nothing if you pay in full and avoid DCC billing.

Samsung Axis Bank Infinite Credit Card

Late payment fees and overdue penalties were restructured to the same new tiers, and the DCC markup rose to 3.5%.

The catch: identical logic to every other card in today's Axis batch.

SpiceJet Axis Bank Voyage Black Credit Card

Standard fee and DCC markup update, along with some terms and conditions housekeeping.

The catch: the usual condition, only a cost if you carry a balance or spend through DCC.

Axis Bank Pride Signature Credit Card

International transaction fee structure and payment due thresholds both moved to the standard new pattern.

The catch: as with the rest, this only bites if you're not paying in full or you spend abroad through DCC billing.

Axis Bank AURA Credit Card

Standard pattern: ₹1,200 for ₹10,001-₹50,000, ₹1,300 above that, DCC markup to 3.5% plus taxes.

The catch: the usual, this is a cost only for balance-carriers and DCC spenders.

Axis Bank Select Credit Card

Beyond the standard fee and DCC changes, this card's spend-exclusion list for its annual fee waiver and EDGE reward points got longer. Gift card spends now join insurance, rent, fuel, education, utilities, telecom, government services, wallet, and gold on the excluded list for the fee waiver. For earning EDGE reward points specifically, Bridge Fees, Road Fees & Tolls were also added to the exclusion list.

The catch: if any of your spend on this card runs through gift cards, tolls, or the other newly excluded categories, that spend no longer counts toward your fee waiver or your reward points. Worth checking your spend mix before you assume you're still on track.

FLIPKART AXIS BANK Credit Card

Standard fee and DCC changes, plus a genuinely useful clarification: Axis now says annual fee waiver spend is calculated by transaction posting date, not the date you actually made the purchase, and recommends hitting your waiver criteria at least 3 working days before your card anniversary to be safe.

The catch: if you've ever cut it close on your fee waiver right up to your card anniversary, this is the reason your last purchase might not have counted. Build in that 3-working-day buffer from now on.

AXIS BANK PRIVILEGE Credit Card

Standard pattern: overdue penalty and DCC markup both moved to the new tiers (₹1,200 for ₹10,001-₹50,000, ₹1,300 above, DCC to 3.5%).

The catch: the usual condition applies here too.

Pine Labs HDFC Bank Credit Card

This card is now marked discontinued and closed to new applications. HDFC's language is reassuring for existing holders: you keep all current features and benefits until you're migrated to a replacement card, whether at reissuance, replacement, or renewal. This is the second Pine Labs co-branded HDFC card to get this tag in two days, the Pine Labs HDFC Bank Pro Credit Card was discontinued the very next day.

The catch: "unaffected for now" has an expiry date built in, it lasts until your next reissuance or renewal, at which point you'll be migrated to whatever HDFC replaces this card with. Keep an eye on that migration notice when it comes.

Retailio HDFC Bank Credit Card

Same discontinuation, same reassurance for existing cardholders: full current benefits continue until migration to a replacement card at reissuance, replacement, or renewal.

The catch: identical to the Pine Labs card above, this is a "for now" situation, not a permanent one.

American Express® Platinum Reserve℠ Credit Card

New welcome gift: 11,000 bonus Membership Rewards points for new cardholders, a meaningfully larger number than the 4,000-point welcome gifts Amex added to its Gold and Membership Rewards cards yesterday.

The catch: as always with Amex welcome gifts, confirm the minimum spend and activation window on the terms page before you count on this.

American Express® Platinum Card

Two things moved on Amex's flagship card. The annual fee is now listed at ₹66,000 plus applicable taxes, and there's a new welcome gift worth up to ₹60,000, with a choice between Taj Hotels credit, a Luxe Gift Card, or The Postcard Hotels & Resorts.

Do the math on whether that's worth it to you: at ₹66,000 plus roughly 18% GST, you're looking at close to ₹78,000 out of pocket in year one, offset by up to ₹60,000 in welcome value if you pick the right redemption. Net cost in year one could be as low as ₹18,000, but only if you actually use the full welcome gift, and only in year one; renewal years don't get that offset.

The catch: this card was never for the mass market, and this update doesn't change that. The math only works if you'll genuinely use the Taj Hotels credit, the gift card, or the Postcard Hotels stay, don't let the "up to ₹60,000" headline number do the deciding for you.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold any of the thirteen standard-pattern Axis cards in today's list, the same rule from yesterday applies: this costs you nothing if you pay your statement in full and avoid DCC-billed transactions. If you don't, set up full autopay and choose local-currency billing where you have the option.

If you hold the Axis Bank Select card, go check your spend mix against the newly excluded categories, gift cards especially, since that's an easy one to miss. If you hold the FLIPKART AXIS BANK card, build a 3-working-day buffer into your annual fee waiver spend from now on instead of cutting it close to your card anniversary.

If you hold either discontinued HDFC card, Pine Labs or Retailio, nothing changes today, but don't assume "for now" means forever, read your migration notice carefully when it arrives.

If you're considering the Amex Platinum Card, do the welcome-gift math honestly before you commit to a ₹66,000-plus-tax annual fee: it only pays for itself in year one if you'll actually use the Taj Hotels, gift card, or Postcard Hotels redemption, and renewal years carry the full fee with no offset.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you make a call on any of this, run it past a professional or at least sleep on it. But this is exactly how I'd think about it if these were my cards.

Monzy
